question: In the bubbling fluidized bed, by what percentage did the measured NO emissions rise when the NH3 co-firing ratio went from 0 to 10% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0?
rendered:
According to the text, the measured NO emissions rose from 169 ppm to 308 ppm as the NH3 co-firing ratio went from 0 to 10% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0. This represents a rise of 308 - 169 = 139 ppm.

To find the percentage increase, divide the rise in NO emissions (139 ppm) by the original NO emissions (169 ppm), and then multiply by 100:

(139 / 169) * 100 = 82.1%

So, the measured NO emissions rose by approximately 82.1% when the NH3 co-firing ratio went from 0 to 10% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0.
